questions.question: Which of the following best describes the significance of Felix Mendelssohnâs 1829 performance of the St. Matthew Passion?
options: It precipitated the Bach Revival.
It was the first performance of the work since Bachâs death.
It established Bach as a court composer for the Elector of Saxony.
It led to the publication of the Bach-Werke-Verzeichnis.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Felix Mendelssohn precipitated the Bach Revival with a performance of the St. Matthew Passion in 1829.
Incorrect. The article does not say this was the first performance since Bachâs death.
Incorrect. The court composer title was granted to Bach by Augustus III in 1736, not connected to Mendelssohnâs performance.

questions.question: Which role did Bach assume in Leipzig in 1723 that made him responsible for music in four Lutheran city churches and the St. Thomas School?
options: Thomaskantor
Court composer of the Elector of Saxony
Organist at the New Church in Arnstadt
Director of the Collegium Musicum
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that by 1723 Bach was hired as Thomaskantor, church music director of Leipzig, responsible for music in four Lutheran city churches and the St. Thomas School.
Incorrect. The title of court composer was granted in 1736 by Augustus III, not the 1723 Leipzig appointment.
Incorrect. The New Church organist post was in Arnstadt in 1703, not Leipzig in 1723.
Incorrect. Bach wrote music for the Collegium Musicum, but that was not the role making him responsible for the four churches and school.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the cultural environment of the Thuringia region where the Bach family lived?
options: Its insular climate fostered conservative musicianship, with external influences arriving mainly via the courts.
It was a cosmopolitan hub that rapidly adopted the latest Italian and French styles.
It discouraged church music in favor of purely secular court entertainment.
It was primarily known for opera production during Bachâs youth.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the Thuringia regionâs insular cultural climate fostered conservative musicianship, with external influences arriving mainly via the courts.
Incorrect. The article describes the climate as insular and conservative, not cosmopolitan.
Incorrect. The article emphasizes church organists and sacred vocal works, not a shift away from church music.
Incorrect. The article does not mention opera production as a feature of Thuringia.

questions.question: If a musicologist wants to study Bachâs contrapuntal techniques such as canon and fugue, which two works cited in the article would be the most directly relevant examples?
options: The Musical Offering and The Art of Fugue
The Brandenburg Concertos and the Cello Suites
The Goldberg Variations and the Toccata and Fugue in D minor
The St. Matthew Passion and the Mass in B minor
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Bachâs mastery of counterpoint is heard in The Musical Offering and The Art of Fugue, and notes many works use contrapuntal techniques like canon and fugue.
Incorrect. These are listed as orchestral and solo instrumental works, not specifically as examples of counterpoint in the article.
Incorrect. The Goldberg Variations is a keyboard work and the Toccata and Fugue is an organ work, but the article specifically names The Musical Offering and The Art of Fugue for counterpoint.

questions.question: Based on the article, which statement best characterizes the trajectory of Bachâs posthumous reputation during the 18th and 19th centuries?
options: He was primarily known as an organist for decades after death, then biographies and complete editions emerged in the 19th century.
He was immediately recognized as the greatest Western composer after his death in 1750.
His music was forgotten until Mendelssohnâs 1829 performance revived interest.
His works were all printed during his lifetime, so no posthumous publication was needed.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that several decades after his death Bach was still primarily known as an organist, and that biographies were published in the 19th century with all known music printed by the end of that century.
Incorrect. The article says acclaim as one of the greatest composers came after the Bach Revival, not immediately after his death.
Incorrect. The article notes continued dissemination through scholarship and publications before Mendelssohn, so interest was not entirely absent.
Incorrect. The article lists works printed during his lifetime but says all known music was printed by the end of the 19th century, implying posthumous publication was needed.

questions.question: Which of the following accurately reflects Bachâs employment situation in Leipzig?
options: He had difficult relations with his employer, somewhat remedied by a court composer title from Augustus III in 1736.
He enjoyed uniformly harmonious relations with the Leipzig city council throughout his tenure.
He was dismissed from the Thomaskantor post after conflicts with the church authorities.
He held the Leipzig position simultaneously with the court composer title from the start in 1723.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Bach had difficult relations with his employer in Leipzig, somewhat remedied when Augustus III granted him the court composer title in 1736.
Incorrect. The article explicitly describes difficult relations, not uniformly harmonious ones.
Incorrect. The article does not say he was dismissed from the Leipzig post.
Incorrect. He was hired in 1723 but received the court composer title in 1736, not at the start.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how Bach incorporated Lutheran hymns into his work?
options: He used them in larger vocal works and also in four-part chorales and sacred songs.
He rejected Lutheran hymns in favor of Latin church music exclusively.
He adapted them only for organ works and never for vocal settings.
He composed Lutheran hymns but did not incorporate them into his own compositions.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Bach adopted Lutheran hymns not only in larger vocal works but also in four-part chorales and sacred songs.
Incorrect. The article says he adopted Lutheran hymns alongside Latin church music, not exclusively Latin.
Incorrect. The article explicitly mentions vocal settings such as chorales and sacred songs, not only organ works.
Incorrect. The article says he adopted existing Lutheran hymns into his works, not that he composed hymns without incorporating them.
